label: ex:benzene-ring
title: Benzene as a molecular Hopf ring $\mathrm{C}_6$
html:
Benzene (\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6) is the prototypical threaded molecular ring: six carbon atoms bound by a single threading link T(2,6).

Construction. The six carbon atoms form the ring \mathcal{R}_6:

  \mathrm{C}_6^{\mathrm{ring}}
  = 
  [\mathcal{A}(6,6)_1, \ldots, \mathcal{A}(6,6)_6]
   \oplus 
  T(2,6).

The threading link T(2,6) has 10 crossings of the same sign.

The two components are the \pi electrons. T(2,6) has two components, each an unknotted loop winding 3 times through all 6 carbons. These components are the two delocalised \pi electrons of benzene. Delocalisation is topological.

Alexander polynomial.

  \Delta_{T(2,6)}(q)
  = 
  q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}
  = 
  (q + q^{-1})^2 - 1.

The crossing energy is proportional to this polynomial, strictly less than the weight of 6 separate Hopf links.

Bond order equalisation. There are no individual bonds — the threading link distributes binding uniformly. Each carbon is threaded identically, producing equal bond lengths and equal bond orders of 3/2.

Hydrogen attachment. T(2,6) consumes 2 sites per carbon. One remaining site bonds to hydrogen, and one participates in the \sigma-backbone. Total hydrogen capacity is 6, giving \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6.

Aromaticity as threading. Aromaticity corresponds to the existence of a threading link. For even N, the threading link is universally twice as efficient as pairwise bonding. The odd-N case requires separate treatment.
